task_text: Generate linear referencing system marks. The script generates a point vector layer containing linear referencing system (LRS) marks (pKs) at fixed intervals (25 m) along an input line/polyline vector layer (e.g., road, river, pipeline axis), then applies a predefined QGIS style (LRS_Style.qml) to visually represent the marks and associated text labels. It uses QGIS Processing’s native 'pointsalonglines' algorithm with zero start/end offsets and a fixed distance of 25 meters, and outputs styled point features for civil engineering or transportation corridor management applications.

Generate synthetic spatial phenomenon. The script generates a synthetic spatial phenomenon over a user-defined study area by creating a hexagonal grid, assigning initial integer values (0–100) to cells based on configurable continuity and smoothness constraints, iteratively adjusting cell values to achieve target 'suavidade' (smoothness) and 'continuidade' (continuity), and finally distributing random points inside grid cells proportional to their assigned values. Outputs include: (1) a vector layer of clipped hexagonal cells with synthetic values ('valor'), auto-incremented IDs, and derived topological attributes; (2) a point layer ('Pontos_aleatorios') where point density per cell reflects the synthetic value (scaled by 'val_max'); and (3) diagnostic results including achieved smoothness and status messages.

Model species range with ineffective barriers. The script calculates the potential distribution range of a species by buffering its known distribution by a user-defined dispersal distance, intersecting that buffer with a reference grid (e.g., administrative units or ecological grid cells), then excluding areas influenced by ineffective zones (e.g., barriers, unsuitable ecosystems) via buffering those zones by an 'ineffective distance' and subtracting the resulting buffered ineffective grids from the initial range grids. The final output is a vector layer ('Range') representing the refined, barrier-adjusted species range at the resolution of the reference grid.

Propagate rupture probabilities along lines. The script computes cascading failure probabilities by combining polygon-based rupture probabilities (e.g., from infrastructure or geological sources) with line-based propagation probabilities (e.g., fault traces, flow paths, or hazard corridors). It spatially splits rupture polygons using propagation lines, identifies which polygon subparts lie left-of each line (using single-sided buffering), and assigns an accumulated probability of occurrence (acca_prob) by indexing into a pre-defined domain matrix (domains.MATRIX_BREAKING) that maps rupture × propagation probability pairs to final event likelihoods. Output is a polygon layer enriched with a 'periodo_ritorno' field and the computed 'acca_prob' per feature.

Fill gibbsite raster bands. The script processes a 10-band input raster named 'RF_Gibbsite.tif', where each band represents a spatial prediction (likely from a Random Forest model) of gibbsite — a clay mineral indicator in soil science. For each band, it extracts the band as a single-band GeoTIFF, then applies GRASS 'r.fill.stats' to fill NoData (void) pixels using inverse-distance-weighted interpolation with distance=3, power=2, and 8-directional search cells; uncertainty rasters ('uc') are simultaneously generated. Finally, all filled bands are merged into two multi-band outputs: 'RF_Gibbsite_filled.tif' (filled predictions) and 'RF_Gibbsite_uc.tif' (filled uncertainty estimates). The workflow is purely raster post-processing — no time-series, no external GEE image collections, no classification or modeling logic — and operates entirely on a precomputed local raster file. Study area, time range, satellite data, and geographic extent are not specified in the code; the only domain-specific clue is the variable name 'Gibbsite', indicating a soil mineralogical target within pedology/soil mapping.

Convert ice-water boundaries to polylines. The script processes pre-classified raster files representing detected ice-water boundaries (stored in 'water_ice/*.tif') and converts them into vector polyline layers. It applies GDAL nodata masking (setting 0 as NoData), GRASS r.thin to skeletonize the binary boundary raster (200 iterations), GRASS r.to.vect to raster-to-vector conversion (line type, value column), and reprojects the resulting shapefiles from an unspecified input CRS to EPSG:3413 (NSIDC Polar Stereographic North, used for Arctic cryosphere applications). The final outputs are reprojected polyline shapefiles named 'wil_edge_line_{counter}.shp' → 'wil_line_repr_{counter}.shp', loaded as vector layers in QGIS. The study area is implied to be a glacier in Oregon (per Dropbox path), and the time range is indicated by the folder '2003/Classified/', confirming data from 2003. No satellite, sensor, or band information is present — the input rasters are already classified outputs ('Classified/edges/water_ice/'), so the script performs post-classification geometric processing only. Input CRS is not specified; output CRS is EPSG:3413 with explicit proj pipeline definition.

Score language overlap proximity. The script computes a linguistic proximity scoring metric for minor language points relative to major language polygons. It first identifies spatial overlaps between minor language points and three categories of major language polygons (both_ab_lng, type_a_lng, type_b_lng), then calculates distances from each point to the boundary of minimal circles enclosing matching type_a language polygons (D) and to the nearest line geometry of those same polygons (b), computes D-b differences, applies a logarithmic transformation (fxa = 21.6679 * ln(101 - 100*(D-b)/D)) per overlap, extracts up to three ISO codes from type_b overlaps (lngb1–lngb3), retrieves corresponding confidence scores ('confidenceB') from an external layer 'Danny_score_e1e6d035_60c8_4fb7_9c0a_da935ec21eea' filtered by country and code, and concatenates them into a final comma-separated 'fxb' field. Output is a vector layer with added scoring fields including 'fxb'.

Plot river transect WSE profiles. The script generates cross-sectional plots of Water Surface Elevation (WSE) along river centerline transects, overlaying multiple RAS (River Analysis System) WSE rasters (e.g., from different storm events or typhoon scenarios like 'Ty. Odette') against a baseline terrain elevation profile. For each input river centerline feature (named, e.g., 'Transect_1'), it samples elevation values at 1-meter intervals, extracts terrain and all matching WSE rasters (via glob pattern 'SB*/WSE*.tif'), constructs distance–elevation arrays, and saves a publication-ready PNG figure showing terrain (black line) and WSE curves (colored lines) with labeled legends (e.g., 'Ty. Odette', 'Ty. Odette-Post'), axis labels ('Station (m)', 'WSE (m)'), and tight layout.

Load SRTM DEM tiles. The script loads SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission) digital elevation model (DEM) raster tiles matching the current QGIS map canvas extent using a prebuilt grid vector layer (srtm_grid.gpkg). It extracts intersecting grid cells, resolves corresponding .hgt filenames, loads valid raster layers from a local folder, and either adds a single raster layer or builds and loads a GDAL virtual raster (VRT) mosaic when multiple tiles are required. Outputs include one or more loaded DEM raster layers named 'DEM' at the bottom of the layer tree, and optionally a missing-tiles vector layer if some SRTM tiles are absent.

Extract land type areas. The script extracts and calculates land system/unit areas for property, paddock, and watered areas using vector polygon layers (land types, paddocks, waterpoints). It transforms layers to a common CRS (EPSG:9473 if input is geographic), dissolves land types by unit field, computes intersections between land types and paddocks/watered buffers (3km/5km), measures areas using ellipsoidal or planar methods, appends area metrics (m², ha, km², %), saves outputs in user-specified vector formats (gpkg/shp/json/kml/kmz), and optionally exports a summary spreadsheet. Outputs include multiple vector layers named e.g., 'Property_land_types', 'Paddock_land_types', 'Paddock_3km_WA_land_types', and an XLSX report.

Generate estuary water area. The script produces a cleaned, filled water area for an estuary by intersecting a manually drawn polygon ('estuario_rascunho') with OpenStreetMap (OSM) water features (natural=water, landuse=reservoir, or waterway=riverbank) extracted from a Geofabrik Brazil South PBF file. It performs geometry cleaning (fix, dissolve, multipart-to-singlepart), reprojection to UTM 22S (EPSG:32722), spatial clipping and filtering by OSM tags, hole removal, and area-based filtering (MIN_WATER_AREA_M2). Outputs include GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, and CSV files containing the final water polygons with attributes (id, name, source, method, area_m2, perim_m).

Generate concave hull from points. The script computes a concave hull (alpha shape) from an input point layer using Delaunay triangulation, edge-length filtering based on an alpha threshold (0–1), removal of triangles with edges longer than alpha × maximum edge length, dissolution of remaining triangles, and optional hole removal and multipart geometry splitting. The output is a polygon vector layer representing the concave hull.

Identify contributing subcatchments. The script identifies the upstream contributing subcatchments for each gauging station by topologically traversing a river network (using NET_ID and NET_TO fields), collecting associated subcatchments via CATCH_ID, dissolving them into a single polygon per station, and attaching Mean Flow and Mean Low Flow attributes from the gauging station layer. It requires pre-processed inputs: a fixed river network with flow direction topology, ungaged subcatchment polygons, and point-based gauging stations with hydrological time-series summary fields (e.g., annual mean flow). Output is a polygon layer — one dissolved gauged subcatchment per station — enriched with flow metrics.

Convert points to polygons. The script converts an input point vector layer into polygon features by first reprojecting the points to EPSG:4326, then connecting them into closed paths (lines) using a grouping field and sequence ordering field, and finally polygonizing those lines into valid polygons. The output is a polygon vector layer ('refatorado') preserving original attributes, intended for representing enclosed areas (e.g., field boundaries, plot perimeters, or administrative zones) derived from ordered boundary points.

Rasterize vector layers over output raster. The script merges multiple vector layers (e.g., administrative boundaries, land use polygons, or constraint zones) from a QGIS project into a single vector layer, then burns a fixed value (0) into the project’s existing output raster using those merged vectors as a mask—effectively restricting or masking the raster to areas covered by the vectors. The output is a modified raster where pixels under the vector geometries retain (or are overwritten with) the burn value, and the merged vector layer is also returned for reference.

Extract municipal land cover and ecosystem layers. The script selects 49 Colombian municipalities by their numeric codes (MPIO_CDPMP) from a national political boundary shapefile (MGN_MPIO_POLITICO.shp), saves the selection as a new vector layer (municipios_seleccionadosp.shp), then performs spatial clipping of two thematic geospatial datasets — 'Ecosistemas' (ecosystem types) and 'Coberturas' (vegetation cover) — first collectively and then individually per municipality. For each municipality, it generates separate GPKG files (e.g., 'Ecosistemas_76109_Buenaventura.gpkg') containing only the portions of those thematic layers intersecting that municipality’s boundary. Outputs include: (1) a consolidated clipped layer for all selected municipalities, and (2) 49 municipally partitioned GPKG files for both ecosystems and vegetation cover, stored in dedicated output directories with sanitized filenames.

Clip ecosystems and vegetation cover by community councils. The script selects specific community councils (by ID) from a titled community council shapefile, then performs spatial clipping of two thematic vector layers—'Ecosistemas' (ecosystems) and 'Coberturas' (vegetation cover)—against each selected council polygon individually. For each council, it generates a separate GeoPackage file containing only the portions of ecosystems and vegetation cover intersecting that council’s boundary. Outputs include: (1) a filtered shapefile of selected councils ('Consejo_seleccionados.shp'), (2) clipped ecosystem layers per council (e.g., 'Ecosistemas_Nombre.gpkg'), and (3) clipped vegetation cover layers per council (e.g., 'Coberturas_Nombre.gpkg'), all saved to dedicated subdirectories and optionally loaded into the QGIS project.

Clip disturbance areas by 2025 area. The script clips a merged disturbance layer ('SL1 BH3 merged disturbance') using a grid and then further clips the gridded output by a dissolved 2025 area calculation layer ('Dissolved 2025 area calc'). It first creates a rectangular polygon grid aligned to the extent of the disturbance layer, with spacing determined by expression '@extent_width' and fixed vertical spacing. Then it clips the disturbance layer by that grid, and finally clips the resulting gridded disturbance features by the dissolved 2025 area polygon layer. The output is a vector feature class ('Clipped output 2025') containing only the portions of the disturbance layer intersecting the 2025 area.

Summarize line length within polygons. The script computes the total (and optionally count, mean, median) length of line features intersecting each polygon in a reference polygon layer, filters out polygons with insufficient total line length (based on user threshold), and outputs a polygon-based summary layer enriched with original polygon attributes. It performs intersection, geometric length calculation in projected CRS, aggregation by polygon ID, and attribute join—producing a vector layer where each feature represents a polygon with zonal line statistics and its original non-ID attributes.

Generate AGOpenGPS section file. The script converts QGIS vector layers (field boundary and weed polygons) into an AGOpenGPS-compatible Sections.txt file. It generates two nested grids (small and large quadrats) within the field boundary, computes the area without weeds via geometric difference, extracts grid cells fully inside the weed-free area, removes large-grid cells already covered by small-grid cells using set difference, merges remaining sections (large-grid patches, small-grid-only patches, and boundary-aligned patches), and exports them as a text file with local-meter coordinates relative to a StartFix origin (read from AGOpenGPS Fields.txt). Each section is written as a 5-line block: number of vertices (5), RGB color, then four 3D points (Easting,Northing,0) in clockwise order (0→3→1→2), derived from polygon vertices converted from WGS84 to local meters using latitude-dependent meter-per-degree scaling. The output Sections.txt is directly loadable into AGOpenGPS to display pre-applied sections.

Download Copernicus land cover product. The script downloads Copernicus Global Land (CGL) products — specifically NetCDF-formatted land surface thematic datasets (e.g., LAI, FAPAR, land cover, soil moisture) — by programmatically navigating the VITO CGL manifest directory structure; it selects the manifest file corresponding to the user-specified product collection and date, identifies the nearest-availability NetCDF file via date parsing in HTML-manifest paths, downloads it, extracts the first geospatial subdataset (e.g., 'lccs_class' or 'LAI_10D'), and converts it to a compressed GeoTIFF with GDAL Translate. Outputs include the final GeoTIFF file and the original downloaded NetCDF URL.

Generate perpendicular transects. The script generates perpendicular line transects along input centerline features at user-specified sampling intervals. It first optionally densifies the centerlines to improve sampling accuracy, then explodes multilines into single-part segments, constructs a networkx graph to model line connectivity and lengths, identifies the longest path in each connected component, and iteratively places perpendicular transects (of specified width) at cumulative distances along that path. Output is a line vector layer of transects, with original attribute fields preserved and optionally an added 'Distance' field representing cumulative distance from path start. No remote sensing data, time series, or classification is involved — it is a pure geometric vector processing tool operating on user-provided line features.

Calculate surface runoff. The script implements the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Curve Number (CN) method to estimate surface runoff (Q in mm), potential retention (S), initial abstraction (Io), runoff coefficient (CE %), infiltration coefficient (CF %), and initial abstraction coefficient (CIo %) for a user-defined study area. It integrates vector layers of soil hydrologic groups and land use/vegetation cover, intersects them to derive combined CN codes, applies antecedent moisture condition (CHA I/II/III) lookup tables to assign CN values, computes S = 254×(100/CN − 1), Io = 0.2×S, and then applies the standard CN runoff equation Q = (P − Io)²/(P + 0.8×S) when P > Io (else Q = 0). Outputs are five thematic vector layers: GeoQ (full attribute result), NC (Curve Number), CE (runoff coefficient), CF (infiltration coefficient), and CIo (initial abstraction coefficient), each styled with predefined QML symbology.

Delineate catchments and compute discharge. The script delineates watersheds and subbasins from a user-provided DEM using WhiteBoxTools (Wang & Liu depression filling, D8 flow routing, Jenson Snap Pour Points, Watershed, Subbasins, LongestFlowpath). It intersects land cover and soil vector layers with subbasins to compute weighted hydrological parameters (CN, Manning’s n, retardance coefficient, runoff coefficient) per subbasin. For each return period (from user-supplied regression CSV), it computes time of concentration (tc) using five empirical methods (Kirpich, Izzard, FAA, SCS Lag, Kinematic Wave), selects the minimum tc, then applies the Rational Method (Q = 0.278 × C × i × A) to compute peak discharge. Outputs a CSV ('basin_summary.csv') containing subbasin ID, area, weighted CN/n/retardance, longest flow path, average slope, return period, runoff coefficient, selected tc (value and method name), rainfall intensity, and peak discharge.

Model rockfall energy propagation. The script implements the DROKA BASIC method to model rockfall hazard propagation from source points across a terrain. It computes a 3D energy cone defined by lateral spreading angle and energy angle, samples terrain elevation at source and potential impact points, calculates the energy line (delta = start_elev − distance × tan(shadow_angle) − final_elev), filters for physically feasible impacts (delta > 0), derives velocity (sqrt(2×g×delta)) and kinetic energy (delta × g × mass / 1000), aggregates results onto a regular grid (cell size configurable), and outputs a point vector layer where each point represents a DTM cell centroid within the affected area, annotated with count of overlapping cones, percent frequency, min/mean/max energy (kJ), and min/mean/max velocity (m/s).

Identify railway junction nodes. The script generates a point layer of railway transport nodes ('Nós transporte ferroviário') by extracting start and end vertices of railway line segments, removing duplicates, counting how many segments meet at each vertex (via spatial join summary), classifying nodes based on connection count (1 = 'fim de via' / end-of-line, 2 = 'pseudo-no' / pseudo-node, ≥3 = 'juncao' / junction), and clipping the result to a user-provided polygonal work area. The output is a vector point layer with attribute 'valor_tipo_no_trans_ferrov' encoding node type as string values '4', '3', or '1' respectively.

Export administrative boundary. The script exports a user-provided vector line layer as an administrative boundary ('fronteira') into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (RECART schema), adding three standardized fields: 'inicio_objeto' (current timestamp), 'valor_estado_fronteira' (a coded state value selected from an enumerated list via get_lista_codigos), and 'data_publicacao' (a user-specified publication date string). The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms 'qgis:refactorfields' to inject these fields, then 'gdal:importvectorintopostgisdatabaseavailableconnections' to append the enriched layer to the 'public.fronteira' table with geometry column 'geometria', primary key 'identificador', and multi-geometry promotion. Input must be 2D line geometry; no raster, satellite, or temporal filtering is performed — it is a pure vector data ingestion and metadata enrichment task.

Export cable transport route segments. The script exports vector line features representing 'Segmento da via por cabo' (cable transport route segments) from a QGIS input layer into a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table named 'seg_via_cabo' in the 'public' schema. It adds a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' with the current time using QgsProcessing's refactorfields algorithm, then imports the modified layer into the RECART geodatabase via GDAL's PostGIS import algorithm. The input must be a 2D line vector layer; no remote sensing, classification, or temporal analysis is performed. Study area, time range, satellite data, and geographic extent are not specified in the code — it is a generic database export tool dependent on user-provided input geometry and preconfigured PostgreSQL connection.

Assign elevation values to polygon vertices. The script processes input polygon vector layers and a digital elevation model (DEM) raster layer to generate two outputs: (1) a point layer containing densified or original polygon vertices with Z-elevation values sampled from the raster, and (2) a polygon layer with a 'Shape_Width' field set to -1 to indicate TUFLOW-compatible TIN polygon formatting. It uses QGIS native algorithms — Densify by Interval (optional), Extract Vertices, Delete Duplicate Geometries, Raster Sampling, Field Calculator (to copy sampled elevations into a 'Z' field), and Retain Fields — ensuring topologically clean, elevation-annotated vertices snapped to the source polygons for TIN generation.

Aggregate route segments by spatial coordinates. The script processes a vector line layer of routes by (1) exploding each line into its constituent segments, (2) grouping segments using a custom spatial key — the concatenation of the minimum x and maximum y coordinate of each segment's geometry (i.e., 'x_min($geometry)-y_max($geometry)'), and (3) computing per-group statistics: a count of features based on a user-specified identifier field and an optional numeric sum (e.g., traffic flux). The output is a new line vector layer where each feature represents a spatially grouped segment with attached count and sum attributes.

Generate sidewalk network from OSM data. The script generates a full sidewalk network (as LineString features in EPSG:4326) within a user-specified bounding box by fetching and processing OpenStreetMap (OSM) road and optional building data. Key workflow steps include: (1) parsing the input extent (QgsRectangle) and transforming it to EPSG:4326; (2) computing a local UTM CRS for internal metric operations; (3) querying OSM Overpass API for highway=* ways using a bbox-based query string with configurable highway type filters (e.g., motorway, residential, footway); (4) cleaning, clipping, and reprojecting fetched road data; (5) assigning street widths (default or per-class); (6) generating protoblocks via polygonization of street networks; (7) filtering protoblocks based on pre-existing sidewalk density (footway=sidewalk); (8) optionally fetching and clipping OSM building footprints for exclusion zone logic; (9) calling the core sidewalk generation function (generate_sidewalk_geometries_and_zones) which produces sidewalk lines, exclusion/sure zones, and width-adjusted streets — all in local TM; (10) generating crossings and kerbs by detecting street endpoint intersections and constructing perpendicular crossing geometries with kerb points at 25% interpolation; and (11) reprojecting final outputs (sidewalks, crossings, kerbs) back to EPSG:4326. Debug layers (protoblocks, exclusion zones, sure zones, width-adjusted streets) are optionally saved in their native CRS (EPSG:4326 for protoblocks, local TM for others). No satellite, sensor, or time-series data is used — inputs are exclusively vector OSM data fetched live via Overpass API.

Topologically correct polygon layer. The script performs topological correction of overlapping polygon layers (TGU, OVTA, WQMP, and Land Use Block) by iteratively resolving geometric relationships—equality, within, and overlap—using spatial joins and geometry difference operations. It applies domain-specific attribute-based tie-breaking rules (e.g., 'TCEffect' for delineations, 'AssessDate' for OVTAs) to determine which feature dominates in overlaps, then subtracts the subordinate geometry from the dominant one. The final output is a non-overlapping, single-part polygon layer ('TGUsNoLines') with cleaned geometries (no line strings, no slivers, area ≥1, and mandatory LUBID/SJID attributes), written as a GeoJSON file.

Extract elevation contour stroke geometry. The script processes a vector layer of elevation contours (selected where elevation modulo 100 equals zero) to generate a stroked polygon representation — i.e., a filled 'line' geometry with user-defined visual thickness. It converts multipart lines to single parts, closes them into polygons, applies an inward negative buffer (scaled by map scale and stroke width), computes the geometric difference between outer and inner buffered polygons to yield a centered stroke geometry, then clips the result to the extent of a raster layer named 'rata_rectangle1'. The final output is a clipped memory vector layer of topographic contour strokes suitable for cartographic rendering at scale ~1:55,000.

Extract river network upstream downstream points. The script extracts upstream (last vertex), downstream (first vertex), and next-to-downstream (second vertex) points from a D8 stream network vector layer clipped to a geographic domain; it then samples upstream accumulation values from a flow accumulation raster at these points, producing five shapefiles: clipped stream network, upstream points (domain and full), downstream points, next-to-downstream points, and their corresponding accumulation-sampled versions — all intended as spatial inputs for LISFLOOD-FP and mizuRoute hydrological modeling.

Extract tent structures in IDP camps. The script identifies tented structures within IDP (Internally Displaced Persons) camps using RGB satellite imagery and sample bare-ground points. It computes soil brightness index (BI) to characterize bare areas, derives spectral ratios (r = R/(R+G+B), g = G/(R+G+B)), constructs fuzzy features f1 (mean absolute deviation of r and g from their respective band values) and f3 (positive part of green minus min(red, blue)), normalizes and thresholds them using Otsu’s method, segments built-up-like pixels, excludes bare areas via inversion and masking, applies binary morphological opening to clean noise, and finally polygonizes the resulting binary mask to output vector polygons representing tented structures — requiring post-processing (e.g., rectanglify, differencing against known camp boundaries) for operational use.

Convert points to polygons. The script converts a selected QGIS vector point layer into a polygon layer by first creating a line path from the points (ordered by a user-selected attribute field), then converting that line to a closed polygon. It computes and adds a 'hectarea' field with area in hectares, applies red outline symbology with transparent fill, and labels each polygon with its area rounded to two decimals (e.g., '12.34 ha.'). Input points must be selected (or all used if none selected), and the ordering field determines path sequence — critical for meaningful polygon topology.

Cluster building polygons by comp_id. The script groups individual building footprint polygons (from a vector layer named 'singlepart_polys') by the attribute 'comp_id', dissolves geometries per group into MultiPolygons, filters out groups with fewer than MIN_COUNT (1) constituent polygons, appends a 'num_features' count field, applies random categorical symbology per comp_id, and exports the result as a styled GeoPackage layer ('Clustered_Groups.gpkg') embedded with renderer metadata. The output is a clustered, attribute-filtered, and visually categorized vector layer of building group envelopes.

Calculate centroid-to-coast distance. The script computes the shortest Euclidean distance from the centroids of dyadic administrative units (‘dyadcells’) to the nearest point on the Natural Earth 10m coastline. It outputs: (1) a shapefile of dyad centroids with coordinates (dyadcentroids.shp), (2) a line vector layer representing the shortest distance from each centroid to the coast (distance.shp), (3) a joined attribute table linking each dyad centroid to its nearest coastal point, and (4) a CSV file (dyadcentroids_closest_coast.csv) containing for each dyad: its ID (cid), centroid latitude/longitude (cent_lat, cent_lon), and the latitude/longitude of the nearest coastal point (coast_lat, coast_lon). The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms including geometry fixing, centroid generation, GRASS v.distance for nearest-point line creation, vertex extraction, attribute joining, and field calculations — all operating on vector inputs only. No remote sensing imagery, time-series, or raster analysis is involved. Study area is implied by input paths and filenames but not geographically bounded in code; data sources are local vector files: Natural Earth 10m coastline and user-provided ‘dyadcells.shp’. No satellite, sensor, or band information is present.

Generate 5-meter hydrographic reference network. The script creates a refined hydrological reference network with a standardized 5-meter width by integrating and processing vector datasets: (1) hydrographic surface polygons (e.g., natural water bodies and reservoirs), (2) an existing reference hydrographic segment network, (3) exutoire (outlet) buffer zones, and optionally (4) a watershed zone boundary. It performs topological network analysis—including node identification, connectivity fixing, network measurement from outlets, Hack and Strahler stream ordering—and applies geometric and attribute-based filters (e.g., minimum length inside water surface ≥30%, removal of isolated Strahler rank 1 segments <500 m connecting to rank ≥3 streams, and elimination of short outlet streams <10,000 m). The final output is a cleaned, topologically consistent, single-width (5 m) linear hydrographic network layer saved as a GeoPackage.

Identify cloud-free wind-calmed areas. The script processes ERA5 reanalysis data ('Total cloud cover' and '10m wind speed') to compute multi-year monthly medians (and optionally standard deviations), applies user-defined thresholds to identify spatially contiguous areas meeting cetacean survey feasibility criteria (e.g., cloud cover ≤ 0.2 or wind speed ≤ 8 m/s), masks results using land (for live cetaceans) or buffered coastline (for stranded cetaceans), and outputs georeferenced raster maps and vector shapefiles ('suitable area(s)') representing optimal optical satellite acquisition zones over water — all tailored per cetacean type (live/stranding), location, data type, and statistic.

Compute least cost path. The script computes a least cost path between two user-specified points using a digital elevation model (DEM) and a friction cost raster. It first runs GRASS r.walk.coords to generate a direction raster based on elevation and friction, then uses GRASS r.drain with that direction raster and reversed start coordinates to trace the optimal path from destination back to source. The output is a vector line layer representing the least cost path.

Calculate urban environmental indicators. The script computes three urban environmental indicators—cooling (rafraichissement), runoff (ruissellement), and biodiversity (biodiversité)—by aggregating classified land cover pixels (10-class EVA or 8-class legacy system) within user-defined calculation zones (parcels or automatically generated 'ilots'). It performs zonal histogram analysis on a classification raster (either input directly or vector-rasterized), computes class-wise percentages and surface areas, then applies fixed per-class coefficients to derive weighted indicator scores per zone. Outputs are a vector layer with attributes 'coef_raf', 'coef_bio', and 'coef_rui' attached to each parcel/ilot polygon, named according to input configuration (e.g., 'Indi_En_V2.2_vec_10_ilot').

Estimate floodwater depth. The script estimates floodwater depth by subtracting a clipped DEM from a distance-transformed flood boundary raster: (1) clips the input DEM to the flood polygon extent; (2) converts the flood polygon to polylines; (3) rasterizes those polylines; (4) extracts DEM elevation values along the rasterized boundary; (5) computes Euclidean distance from the boundary to interior cells using GRASS r.grow.distance; (6) calculates gross water depth as the difference between the distance-derived surface (interpreted as water surface elevation proxy) and the underlying DEM; (7) applies a Gaussian filter to smooth the resulting depth raster; and outputs a filtered flood depth raster (waterDepthFiltered.sdat). The methodology assumes inland riverine flooding and relies on topographic gradients to infer water surface slope from the inundation boundary.

Identify basin areas using slope-based concave hulls. The script identifies potential basin areas by first applying a slope high-pass filter to a digital slope raster (e.g., derived from DEM), then sampling filtered slope values at regularly spaced points within a user-defined extent, and finally generating concave and convex hulls around points where the filtered slope equals 1 (i.e., steep terrain). It outputs reclassified slope rasters, sampled point shapefiles, and polygon shapefiles (concave/convex hulls) enriched with zonal statistics (e.g., mean, max slope) — enabling identification of topographically enclosed low-lying areas partially bordered by inclined terrain.

Generate pedestrian walksheds from transit stops. The script generates walkshed polygons (buffered, network-constrained, concave-hull refined, and route-dissolved) for public transit stops using a pedestrian street network. It processes stops grouped by 'rte' (route ID), computes service areas via QGIS native network analysis ('serviceareafromlayer'), refines geometry using convex and concave hulls, clips and dissolves by route, and outputs GeoPackage files for walksheds, dissolved walksheds, and service area lines — all batched to manage memory.

Unify isochrone polygons with derived boundaries. The script processes an input vector layer of isochrone polygons by first converting them to lines, then polygonizing those lines to create new polygons (likely filling gaps or holes), and finally performing a union operation between the original isochrone polygons and the newly polygonized features. The output is a unified vector layer where overlapping or adjacent geometries are merged, preserving all attributes from both inputs, intended to produce a topologically consistent boundary representation of the isochrone area.

Dissolve parcels by zoning. The script processes a QGIS vector layer named 'fbc-parcels', dissolving its features based on the 'fbc_zoning' attribute field, then converts the resulting multipart geometries into single-part features. The output is a new in-memory vector layer named 'fbc_large_zones' added to the QGIS project, representing spatially contiguous zones grouped by zoning classification.

Classify urban polygon changes by density type and comparison category. The script performs a combinatorial attribute-based classification and spatial processing of an input vector layer named 'poligonos', filtering features by three categorical fields: 'Densidade' (e.g., 'Densa', 'Pouco densa', 'Loteamento vazio'), 'Tipo' (e.g., 'Área Urbanizada', 'Vazio intraurbano'), and 'Comparacao' (e.g., 'Adição', 'Densificação', 'Subtração'). For each unique combination, it selects matching polygons, executes a spatial self-join (using 'contains' predicate), dissolves the resulting geometries, and splits multi-part polygons into single parts — exporting each result as a separate shapefile named 'poligonos_<Densidade>_<Tipo>_<Comparacao>.shp'. The output is a set of 132 (3×4×11) georeferenced, topologically cleaned, single-part polygon layers representing distinct urban change–density–land use categories.

Map solar radiation distribution. The script processes precomputed solar radiation raster files (e.g., '2020_Average.tif', monthly 'YYYY_MM.tif') by clipping them to Brazil’s national boundary (BR_Pais_2021.shp), applying Turbo pseudocolor rendering with 255 classes, and generating publication-ready PNG maps (800×800 px) that include dynamic min/max value labels, month abbreviation label, and units ('kWh/m²/day'). It uses QGIS layout export to produce georeferenced, styled visualizations for time-series solar radiation assessment over Brazil — no GEE server-side computation occurs; the script is purely a QGIS desktop automation workflow for raster styling, clipping, and map composition.

Compare road network lengths. The script computes and compares the total length of two input line vector layers (Road Network 1 and Road Network 2) within each polygon feature of a user-provided region layer, using the region’s ID field for spatial aggregation. It runs the 'Road Network Length' model twice (once per road network) to obtain summed line lengths per region, joins the two resulting length tables on the Region ID field, and calculates a new field 'lenDIFF' as the difference ('length' − 'length_2') between the two networks’ lengths per region. The output is a vector layer (polygon or geometry-agnostic) containing the original region geometries plus attributes: region ID, length of Road Network 1, length of Road Network 2, and their difference.

Calculate sediment retention volume. The script calculates the sediment retention volume (stauraum) of a debris retention basin by generating an artificial 3D surface from a user-defined query line (Abfragelinie), its height (Sperrenhoehe), and a sedimentation gradient (Verlandungsgefaelle). It clips a high-resolution ALS-derived DGM (1 m) to a buffer around the line, extracts elevation profiles, computes minimum terrain elevation (ZMIN), constructs a 3D polygon representing the theoretical retention surface, interpolates it into a TIN raster, subtracts it from the clipped DGM to produce a difference raster (positive values = retained volume), sums pixel-wise positive volume contributions (cell size × absolute value), and outputs both the total volume (in m³) and a smoothed, simplified polygon layer ('stauraum.shp') representing the inundated/retained area. The workflow includes automated labeling, symbology (blue fill), and layer grouping in QGIS.

Sample air quality raster values at urban agricultural points. The script samples raster pixel values from a collection of air quality rasters (stored in ESRI Grid format, .adf) at fixed urban agricultural point locations in New York City. It reprojects both the rasters and the point layer to EPSG:26918 (NAD83 / UTM zone 18N), performs point-in-raster sampling using QGIS’s native:rastersampling algorithm, and appends each raster’s sampled values as a new column (named using folder basename + '_sample') to a base DataFrame containing selected attribute fields from the original point layer. The final output is a CSV table with point geometry attributes plus one column per air quality raster, enabling spatially referenced statistical analysis or modeling of exposure.

Estimate air quality exposure using 300m buffer zonal statistics. The script estimates mean air quality exposure values for random points across NYC by computing zonal statistics (mean) of air quality rasters (AnnAvg_1_15_300m) over 300-meter buffers around each point. It reprojects both the input raster stack (NYCCAS annual average air quality surfaces at 300m resolution) and the point layer (nyc_moua_random_points) to EPSG:26918, applies buffering, performs zonal statistics, and appends the resulting mean values as new columns (e.g., 'AnnAvg_1_15_300m_buffer_300m') to a base DataFrame containing original point attributes — ultimately exporting a CSV table linking each random point to its buffered air quality exposure estimate.

Generate multiscale riparian and circular buffers. The script automates the generation of multi-scale spatial buffers—both circular (around point-based field collection sites) and riparian (along linear water features)—using adaptive, spreadsheet-driven parameters. It detects and matches site-specific polygons (e.g., watersheds, contribution areas) to collected points via ID field matching; clips buffers to those polygons; classifies resulting buffers as either valid 'Local Contribution Areas' (LCA) or 'extrapolated areas' based on area comparison with the source polygon; optionally applies difference operations (e.g., removing river lines from riparian buffers); and outputs georeferenced shapefiles organized in a hierarchical directory structure (e.g., '1BUFFER_CIRCULAR', '7RB_Temporary', '9RBLCA'). All results are loaded into QGIS with standardized symbology for visual interpretation.

Convert PGA contours to Ia raster. The script converts earthquake agency-provided KML-formatted PGA (Peak Ground Acceleration) isoline files into georeferenced Ia (Arias Intensity) GeoTIFF rasters. It parses KML Placemarks containing PGA values (e.g., '0.02g'), converts them to physical acceleration (m/s²), computes Ia using the empirical log-linear relationship log₁₀(Ia) = 0.797 + 1.837·log₁₀(PGA), reprojects coordinates to an automatically selected UTM zone (EPSG:326xx), samples and deduplicates contour points, then applies QGIS Processing IDW or TIN interpolation to generate a continuous Ia.tif surface; optionally outputs a polygon-based PGA.tif raster via OGR vector-to-raster conversion.

Download and merge DTM tiles. The script fetches Digital Terrain Model (DTM) files from the Welsh Government LiDAR Tile Catalogue (2020–2023) via a WFS endpoint using the bounding box of a user-selected QGIS vector polygon layer in EPSG:27700. It downloads HTTP-linked DTM GeoTIFFs for a selected year, merges them into a single raster using GDAL merge, and optionally clips the merged raster to the input polygon boundary using GDAL cliprasterbymasklayer. The final output is loaded as a valid QgsRasterLayer into the QGIS project. Study area is implicitly constrained to Wales (via datamap.gov.wales domain and EPSG:27700 — British National Grid), time range is 2020–2023 per catalogue name, and data source is airborne LiDAR-derived DTM (no satellite/sensor — ground-based active remote sensing).

Download and package provincial OSM shapefiles. The script downloads the latest OpenStreetMap (OSM) shapefile archive for a selected Dutch province from Geofabrik's Europe/Netherlands server, extracts all .shp files, reclassifies them by geometry type (point/line/polygon) via WKB type codes (1/5/6), writes them to renamed shapefiles in a temporary directory, then packages all into a single GeoPackage (.gpkg) file named after the province. It additionally attempts to apply QML/SLD styling from a local 'styling/' subdirectory using layer style metadata stored in the GeoPackage's 'layer_styles' table. The study area is limited to one of the twelve provinces of the Netherlands, specified at runtime via the 'provincie' parameter. No satellite, sensor, or time-series data is used; the source is static vector data from OSM.

Identify local summit points. The script identifies local summit (peak) points within user-defined buffer zones around input point features, using a digital elevation model (DEM). It resolves conflicts where multiple buffers overlap and a single summit falls within more than one buffer by iteratively refining the search area: for conflicting summits, it computes the minimal distance from the summit to the original source points, creates smaller dual-point buffers at that distance, re-runs summit detection in those refined areas, and merges the new, non-conflicting summits into the final output layer. The final output is a vector layer of unique, non-duplicated summit points, each associated with its nearest input point (via the provided or auto-generated ID field), along with intermediate files saved to a user-specified folder.

Generate county-level buffer zones. The script processes a point dataset (Test.txt) containing longitude and latitude coordinates to create three concentric variable-distance buffers (64Distance, 50Distance, 34Distance) around each point. It then computes ring-shaped difference layers (64kt−50kt, 50kt−34kt) and clips each buffer or ring to U.S. county boundaries (cb_2015_us_county_5m.shp), producing three clipped polygon outputs: one for the full 64-knot buffer area, one for the 50–64 knot annulus, and one for the 34–50 knot annulus. The study area is explicitly limited to U.S. counties; the input point data appears related to tropical cyclone wind radii (given field names '64Distance', '50Distance', '34Distance' — standard Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind radii thresholds in nautical miles), suggesting hazard exposure mapping. No satellite, temporal, or spectral analysis is performed; all operations are vector-based GIS workflows in QGIS via PyQGIS. Outputs are shapefiles: temp_clip1.shp, temp_clip2.shp, temp_clip3.shp.

Aggregate CSV addresses by administrative polygons. The script reads a CSV file containing address records, joins them to a polygon vector layer (e.g., administrative boundaries) based on a shared address field, computes counts per polygon (implicitly via join + optional aggregation — though the current logic lacks explicit count aggregation and instead relies on downstream use of joined attributes; however, the plugin name 'Stat_CSVAddressPolygon' and description 'CSV住所別集計(行政界別)' confirm its purpose is statistical aggregation of CSV address occurrences per administrative polygon), and outputs a georeferenced vector layer (e.g., GeoPackage or other format) with joined attributes — including a 'snum' field initialized/updated to 0 where null, suggesting it is intended to hold summary counts. The workflow includes CSV parsing (with encoding selection), spatial join, packaging, NULL handling in SpatiaLite, and optional reprojection.

Analyze ground parrot movement distance. The script analyzes Ground Parrot (Pezoporus wallicus) species movement patterns between consecutive years from 2000 to 2019 by computing Euclidean distances between annual mean centroid coordinates of occurrence records. It uses pre-fire ground parrot point records (with STARTDATE field), clips them to the East Gippsland study area (EPSG:7855 → EPSG:3111), extracts year integers from STARTDATE, filters out records before 2000 and null years, splits the layer by YEAR, computes mean coordinates per year (one point per year), then calculates inter-annual distances using QGIS distance matrix (nearest neighbor, single-source-to-single-target). Outputs are individual shapefiles containing distance attributes (e.g., Mean_dist_2000_2001.shp), visualized as vector layers in QGIS. No satellite or remote sensing data is used; all inputs are local vector shapefiles: east_gippsland.shp (study boundary), pre_fire_gp.shp (occurrence points), hist_fire.shp, post_fire_gp.shp, and heath.shp (wet heathland habitat). The CRS transformation note confirms use of GDA2020 MGA Zone 55 (EPSG:7855) source data, reprojected to EPSG:3111 (VICGRID94) for analysis.

Compute persistent diagram from vector features. The script computes a persistent homology diagram (0-dimensional) from point, line, and polygon vector features loaded from QGIS layers named 'кладбище 1', 'кладбище 2', 'кладбище 3' (Russian for 'cemetery 1/2/3'). It extracts vertex coordinates from geometries (points, polylines, polygons), constructs a point cloud, computes a persistence diagram using an external module (my_import.persistent_diagram), selects a persistence threshold based on the count_object parameter to isolate topological components (e.g., connected components), connects points within that threshold, assigns group IDs, draws resulting points and lines in QGIS layers 'persistent_points' and 'persistent_lines', then performs geometric post-processing: dissolving lines, polygonizing line networks, dissolving individual polygons, detecting spatial relationships (intersection, containment) among resulting polygons, and merging all final polygons into a single output layer. The workflow is purely vector-based and topological — no raster or satellite data is used; inputs are local QGIS vector layers with no georeferencing metadata visible in code. Study area is implied by layer names ('cemetery') but no coordinate system, CRS, or projection is specified or enforced.

Calculate intersection kilometerage for infrastructure projects. The script computes the kilometerage range (e.g., '12+345 - 15+678') along a linear reference layer ('km', interpreted as a kilometer-marked linear infrastructure such as a road or rail alignment) that intersects with clipped and decomposed polygons representing investment areas ('inw'), buffered by a polygonal corridor ('pas'). It derives this by extracting vertices of clipped investment geometries, computing nearest-point distances to 'km' points (assumed to be chainage-marked nodes), aggregating min/max chainage IDs per investment segment, formatting them into human-readable kilometerage strings, joining results back to original investment features, and optionally computing distance-to-nearest-km-line. Output is a vector layer ('WYNIK') enriched with 'wynik_km' (formatted kilometerage range or fallback 'km' field) and 'wynik_dist_pas' (distance from investment centroid to nearest km line).

Adjust parcel block geometry. The script performs parcel block adjustment (Adumanis) — a geospatial adjustment method for cadastral parcel boundaries using control points and least-squares estimation. It processes MultiPolygon vector layers representing land parcels grouped by 'BlockId', identifies geometric nodes (corners), matches coincident or proximal nodes across parcels into tie groups, incorporates control points from a MultiLineString layer (interpreted as begin/end points of control lines), builds observation and design matrices (A and F), solves for affine transformation parameters per parcel via least squares, computes posterior variance, generates error ellipses for adjusted tie points, optionally snaps non-control vertices to nearby segments, and outputs adjusted MultiPolygon layers with pre-/post-adjustment area comparison, centroid layers, and point layers with error ellipse parameters (Sv, Su, t, eX, eY). All outputs are memory layers added to a named group in the QGIS project.

Map wildfire footprints from satellite fire detections. The script processes FIRMS CSV fire detection data (VIIRS and MODIS) for Monchique (2018) and Portugal/Europe (July 2022) to generate georeferenced fire footprint polygons, compute per-pixel FRP per km² (frpkm2), assign decimal and integer acquisition day attributes, and create graduated symbology legends by acquisition time. It reads delimited-text CSVs with longitude/latitude, clips detections to a Portuguese administrative boundary (CAOP 2020), computes footprints using sensor-specific scan/track dimensions and orbital azimuths (VIIRS: 346°, MODIS Aqua: 346°, MODIS Terra: 193°), and optionally dissolves footprints by day. Outputs include vector layers of point detections (‘af’), footprint polygons (‘footprints’ or ‘footprints_K100’), instrument-separated layers (‘viirs_footprints’, ‘modis_footprints’), and graduated legends keyed to acquisition day. No raster outputs, classification models, or time-series analysis are performed — only geometric derivation and attribute enrichment.

Convert GPS points to linear path. The script converts a CSV file containing latitude and longitude columns into a point shapefile (EPSG:4326), then connects those points in sequence (without closing the path) to generate a polyline shapefile representing a trajectory or route. The workflow uses QGIS Processing algorithms 'native:createpointslayerfromtable' and 'native:pointstopath', with no spatial filtering, temporal analysis, classification, or remote sensing operations. Input CSV structure is inferred to contain 'Latitude' and 'Longitude' fields; output files are written to fixed local paths on Windows. No study area, time range, satellite data, or geospatial analysis beyond vector geometry generation is present — it is purely a tabular-to-vector conversion pipeline.

Map households near evacuation centers. The script processes household location data (from a CSV with latitude/longitude) and evacuation center point features (filtered by specific DRRM-related subtype or SPECTYPE values) within a municipal boundary. It reprojects the household points to UTM Zone 51N (EPSG:32651), extracts evacuation centers matching designated emergency site criteria, buffers them by 1 km (dissolved), and identifies which households fall within those buffers. Outputs include: (1) a 1-km buffered polygon layer of evacuation centers, (2) the original household points layer, (3) the filtered evacuation center points layer, and (4) the subset of households spatially within the 1-km buffer — all styled with predefined QML files for visualization in QGIS.

Map senior citizens living alone. The script visualizes senior citizens living alone as point features derived from a CSV table containing latitude and longitude coordinates, overlaid on a city/municipality administrative boundary layer. It loads two input layers: (1) a CSV file ('input_f2_csv') with 'latitude' and 'longitude' fields used to generate points in EPSG:4326, and (2) a polygon vector layer ('input_citymun_boundary') representing city/municipality administrative boundaries. The workflow includes creating a points layer from the CSV, loading both layers into the QGIS project, and applying pre-defined QML style files ('4. CityMun_AdmBdry.qml' and '6. SC Living Alone.qml') for cartographic visualization. No geospatial analysis, classification, or temporal processing is performed — the script is purely for data loading and styling. Study area, time range, satellite/sensor/bands, and classification methods are not specified.

Fuse multisensor optical bands. The script performs sensor-specific band fusion: (1) For Landsat 8, it applies GDAL pansharpening to fuse 30 m multispectral bands B4 (Red), B5 (NIR), B6 (SWIR-1) with 15 m panchromatic band B8, producing a sharpened 15 m RGB-like composite; (2) For Landsat 5, CBERS-4A, and Sentinel-2, it builds virtual rasters stacking specified bands in defined spectral order (B3-B4-B5 for L5; B5-B4-B3 for CBERS-4A; B11-B8-B4 for S2) without sharpening, preserving native resolutions (30 m, ~64 m, and mixed 10/20 m respectively); all outputs are reprojected to a user-specified CRS (default EPSG:4674). The result is a single georeferenced, multi-band raster optimized for visual interpretation or downstream analysis.

Clean polygon topology. The script repairs invalid polygon geometries, harmonizes shared boundaries between adjacent polygons, removes spurious vertices based on short-edge, near-collinearity, and proximity to an optional outline layer, enforces per-feature area-change limits during internal cleanup, and optionally snaps outer boundaries to a reference outline — all without auto-committing changes, writing results to the layer’s edit buffer. It operates on a user-specified input polygon layer (e.g., 'voronoi_topology_errors') and an optional outline layer (e.g., 'Outline'), using QGIS native algorithms ('native:fixgeometries', 'native:snapgeometries') and custom local vertex cleanup logic. No satellite, temporal, or external geospatial data sources are involved; inputs are vector layers already loaded in the QGIS project. Outputs include updated geometries in the edit buffer, plus a printed topology report (invalid count, vertex count, area change, forced moves, etc.).

Extract elevation profile along path. The script generates an elevation profile by sampling a WCS-served digital height model (DHM) along user-selected line features. It first creates a minimal buffer around the input line, loads the DHM raster layer via a WCS endpoint (using an API token), samples elevation values at regularly spaced points along the line (distance interval set by user), computes cumulative distance from the start point, and outputs both a memory vector layer of sampled points with elevation and distance attributes, and a graphical elevation-distance plot via PlotDialog.

Scale Sentinel-2 L1C to TOA reflectance. The script processes a local Sentinel-2 Level-1C product (MSIL1C) by applying the official scaling factor (0.0001) to convert digital numbers (DN) in bands B01, B02, B03, B04, B05, B06, B07, B08, B11, and B12 into top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance values; it then resamples all non-10m bands (B01 at 60m, B05–B07 and B11–B12 at 20m) to 10 m resolution using nearest-neighbor resampling, merges them into a single 10 m multiband GeoTIFF, assigns descriptive band names (e.g., 'Blue', 'NIR', 'SWIR2'), and cleans up temporary files.

Perform polygon identity overlay. The script emulates ArcGIS's Identity tool for polygon layers by computing three geometric operations: (1) Intersection between input and identity layers, preserving attributes from both with 'id_' prefix for identity fields; (2) Difference (input minus identity) to extract portions of the input layer not overlapping the identity layer; and (3) Merge of the intersection and difference results into a single output polygon layer. It supports configurable attribute handling for the identity layer — either all fields, only a user-specified ID field (with prefix 'id_'), or none — via field deletion logic. The final output is a topologically consistent polygon layer where input features are split along identity boundaries, with attributes propagated conditionally.

Generate surface water elevation raster. The script generates a high-resolution digital terrain model (DTM) of the water surface (Surface Libre) from TELEMAC2D hydrodynamic simulation point outputs. It filters points by minimum water depth threshold, joins surface elevation values to those points, reprojects and adds XY coordinates, refactors fields to standard X/Y/Z_w format, converts to LAS point cloud via intermediate TXT, and finally interpolates a raster using LAStools' blast2dem with user-defined resolution and -kill parameter. The output is a GeoTIFF raster representing the maximum water surface elevation (MNSL) across the simulated domain.

Extract hill segments from roads. The script processes road centerlines to identify and extract hill segments—defined as road sections with net grade exceeding a user-defined minimum grade (default 2.5%)—by draping elevation from a Digital Elevation Model (DEM), computing climb/descent per segment, calculating net grade and height, filtering short segments (if enabled), and outputting vector features representing individual uphill or downhill hill segments (dissolved by direction and road name, then split into single parts) with attributes: 'name' (road name), 'direction' (1=uphill, 0=downhill), 'length', 'height', 'grade_net', and 'CAT' (grade_net × height). The workflow includes buffering/reprojecting the DEM extent for spatial alignment, densifying and splitting roads, z-draping, grade computation, directional classification, and attribute cleanup.

Correct PPK tag elevations. The script processes GNSS-derived PPK (Post-Processed Kinematic) point positions (eventpos), samples a geoid height raster (geoideenformatoraster) at each point, and computes orthometric height by subtracting the geoid undulation (REDNAP1) from the ellipsoidal height (height(m)). It also constructs a standardized photo naming convention, populates orientation placeholders (phi/omega/lambda), and computes horizontal/vertical precision metrics (p_h, p_v) conditioned on GNSS solution quality (Q). The output is a reprojected and styled vector layer (PPK_tags) containing corrected heights and metadata suitable for photogrammetric control or UAV survey QA/QC.

Calculate earthwork volumes. The script computes cut-and-fill earthwork volumes by differencing pre- and post-construction digital elevation models (DEMs) within a user-defined area polygon. It clips both DEMs to the area at a specified resolution, calculates three raster layers: total difference (POST − PRE), terra (positive difference = fill/volume added), and desmo (negative difference = cut/volume removed). Zonal statistics sum pixel values per polygon feature, then converts sums to volumetric units (m³) using resolution² scaling. Optionally applies bulk density to compute mass (tons). Outputs a vector layer with fields TOTAL (net volume m³), TERRA (fill m³), DESMO (cut m³), and TONS (mass if density provided), styled with predefined QML files.

Extract land system unit areas. The script extracts and calculates land system/unit areas for property-level (dissolved paddocks), paddock-level, and watered-area-level (3km and/or 5km buffers around waterpoints) geometries. It spatially intersects a land types polygon layer (e.g., land systems or mapping units) with user-provided paddock polygons and optionally dissolved paddocks or buffered waterpoint zones, computes area metrics (m², ha, km², % of parent geometry) using either ellipsoidal (geodesic) or planar measurement, preserves selected attribute fields from the land types layer, and outputs vector layers in user-specified formats (GPKG, SHP, etc.). An optional Excel summary report aggregates all output layers’ attributes and geometry-derived area statistics.

Shred vector or raster layer into grid pieces. The script shreds an input QGIS vector or raster layer into a user-specified number (2–10) of spatially disjoint pieces using a grid-based partitioning approach. It supports three modes: vertical strips (equal-width columns), horizontal strips (equal-height rows), or square tiles (grid with equal spacing in both dimensions). For vector inputs, it clips features per grid cell and saves each as a separate shapefile; for raster inputs, it uses GDAL’s mask-based clipping to extract sub-rasters. Optionally, it applies random spatial shuffling (translation) of the shredded pieces — either pure permutation of positions or collage-style jittered repositioning — before adding all outputs to the QGIS project. The original input layer is removed, and temporary grid layers are cleaned up.

QGIS workflow: Data processing, Vector spatial analysis. This workflow contains 7 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Vector spatial analysis, Data editing. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Simplify forest stand boundaries. The script post-processes raw forest stand boundary polygons (from a TBk classification) by eliminating small polygons (based on area_m2 < min_area), simplifying geometry using GRASS v.generalize with Douglas-Peucker method (tolerance = simplification_tolerance), re-eliminating newly small polygons after simplification, recalculating area_m2 for all features, and updating hmax and hdom attribute values for 'remainder' type polygons using hmax_eff and hp80 fields. Outputs include a cleaned and simplified GeoPackage ('stands_simplified.gpkg'), a temporary highest-tree point layer derived from 'hmax.tif', and intermediate buffers and reduced layers. All operations are vector-based and rely on QGIS processing algorithms.

Create LiDAR base data rasters. The script processes airborne LiDAR point clouds to generate rasters for ground point density, low vegetation density, a digital elevation model via TIN gridding, and an IDW interpolation. First, if not classified, it classifies the point cloud. It then optionally converts LAZ to LAS. Using WhiteboxTools LidarPointDensity, it computes ground point density (excluding non-ground classes) and low vegetation density (excluding other classes). It also runs LidarTINGridding and LidarIdwInterpolation for DEM and IDW. Each raster is resampled to the specified cell size and warped to the target CRS. Finally, these rasters are loaded into the QGIS project if their respective checkboxes are enabled.

Hybrid DFM interpolation from IDW and TLI. The script performs hybrid interpolation of a digital feature model (DFM) by blending inverse distance weighting (IDW) and triangulation with linear interpolation (TLI) raster inputs based on a DFM confidence map. It resamples all inputs to a common cell size, reclassifies the confidence map into low and high confidence zones, grows the high-confidence areas, and uses a raster calculator to combine TLI and IDW rasters with the weighted zones. The resulting hybrid DFM is patched with the TLI where only one method exists, reprojected, and optionally loaded into QGIS. This yields a seamless hybrid DFM that prioritizes TLI in high-confidence areas and IDW in low-confidence areas.

Calculate country areas. The script computes the area in square kilometers for each country from the Natural Earth Admin 0 Countries shapefile. It first drops unnecessary attribute fields, reprojects the geometries to World Cylindrical Equal Area (ESRI:54034), fixes geometries, and then calculates the area using the field calculator. The result is exported as a CSV file with country attributes and area column.

Calculate water depth from airborne lidar. The script processes an ALB (Airborne Laser Bathymetry) point cloud (.vpc) to generate: (1) a 1m-resolution water surface raster (Classification=2 OR 41), (2) a 1m-resolution topobathy DTM (Classification=2 OR 40), (3) water depth raster (DTM subtracted from water surface), (4) 1m water depth contour lines at 1m intervals, (5) a 2m-resolution density raster (points/m² for Class 2/40), (6) a binary mask where density ≥20 AND water depth ∈ [0.5,2.5] m, and (7) a final 2m-resolution raster 'topobathy_2m_density_OK_at_2m.tif' representing areas meeting both density and depth criteria.

Derive watershed basin from DEM and discharge point. The script computes the upslope drainage basin for a user-specified discharge point using a filled DEM and SAGA GIS 'upslopearea' algorithm. It then converts the resulting raster basin to vector (polygonized), fixes geometries, dissolves features, filters to retain only the target watershed, clips the DEM to that basin, generates contour lines at 100 m intervals, clips the input channel network to the basin boundary, and computes watershed-level statistics and Curve Numbers (CN) by intersecting with soil and Corine land cover layers. Outputs include: (1) raw and filtered basin polygons (GPKG), (2) clipped basin DEM (GeoTIFF), (3) 100-m contour lines (GPKG), (4) basin-restricted channel network (GPKG), (5) CN-weighted polygon layer (GPKG), and (6) Corine and SCS land use classification layers (GPKG).

Koppel overige bronnen. The script performs spatial joining and aggregation of infrastructure and utility datasets to a drainage basin (bemalingsgebieden) layer. It counts and sums attributes from four input layers: (1) BAG verblijfsobjecten (VBOs) intersecting each basin (count only), (2) VE's (water utility installations) intersecting each basin (count and sum of 'GRONDSLAG'), (3) Drinkwater connections (sum and count of 'zak_result' and 'par_result'), and (4) Plancap polygons (with calculated PC_ID), which are intersected with basins to compute ExAFW values (ExAFW_2124, ExAFW_2529, ExAFW_3039, ExAFW_4050) per basin via area-weighted aggregation after deduplication and ordering by area. Outputs include summary statistics per basin ID (BEM_ID), detection of basins containing multiple plancaps, plancaps overlapping multiple basins, and joined attribute tables for further analysis in the GeoDynGemGWSW workflow.

Export watercourse area to database. The script prepares polygon watercourse area data for the RECART hydrographic database by adding metadata fields (timestamp and known delimitation boolean) and then exports the layer to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS table 'curso_de_agua_area' using a configured connection.

Export watercourse axis to database. The script exports a vector line layer representing watercourse axes to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. It first refactors the input layer by adding required attribute fields (timestamp, watercourse value, vertical position, delimitation known flag, fictitious flag) based on user parameters. Then it imports the processed layer into the table 'curso_de_agua_eixo' in the 'public' schema using GDAL's import vector into PostGIS tool.

Export hydrographic nodes to PostgreSQL. The script exports hydrographic node point features to a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database table 'no_hidrografico'. It refactors the input layer by adding a timestamp field 'inicio_objeto' and a 'valor_tipo_no_hidrografico' field derived from either a predefined enumeration or a user-selected attribute. The processed layer is then imported into the 'no_hidrografico' table using GDAL's import vector into PostGIS algorithm.

Unsupervised K-means object-based image classification. The script performs unsupervised object-based image classification using K‑means clustering and sieving. It rescales up to five input raster layers to 0–254, builds a multi‑band virtual raster, applies OTB KMeansClassification with a user‑specified number of clusters, removes segments smaller than a user‑defined minimum size with gdal:sieve, converts the result to polygons, aggregates polygons by class value, computes zonal statistics (mean and standard deviation) of the rescaled input bands for each polygon, splits multipart polygons to single parts, and outputs a categorized shapefile with random colors. A textual log file is also generated recording input filenames and parameters.

Generate Curve Number from Soils and Land Cover. The script generates a curve number (CN) vector layer by intersecting soil and land cover layers, computing a combination field (grid_code), and joining with a lookup table to assign CN values. It uses QGIS processing algorithms (intersection, field calculator, join attributes table, delete column). The output is a vector layer with CN attribute for hydrologic modeling.

Download Copernicus Global Land Cover. This QGIS processing plugin downloads Copernicus Global Land Cover data (version 3.0.1) from the vito.landcover.global S3 bucket. The user selects product type, year, and optionally a spatial extent; the algorithm lists available objects, filters by selection, and downloads the corresponding GeoTIFF files to a local directory.

Generate road-based subnet service areas. The script computes network-based allocation zones from point facilities (e.g., substations, access points) along a road network using GRASS v.net.alloc, then constructs Voronoi polygons from sampled vertices of the allocated network segments to produce dissolved polygonal service areas ('subnet_areas') associated with each input point. Key steps include: (1) GRASS v.net.alloc to assign road segments to nearest points within 500m threshold; (2) exploding lines and extracting vertices; (3) aggregating segment geometry length per point ID ('cat'); (4) computing adjusted segment midpoints and endpoints via trigonometric field calculations using angle_at_vertex and centroid; (5) reconstructing oriented line geometries; (6) extracting unique vertex coordinates rounded to 0.1m precision; (7) generating Voronoi polygons from deduplicated vertices; and (8) dissolving by 'cat' (point ID) to yield final subnet area polygons.

Buffer vector features to raster. The script buffers input vector features by a user-specified distance, dissolves the resulting polygons, and rasterizes the buffered layer using a specified cell size. Outputs include a vector buffer layer (BUFFER_OUTPUT), a raster layer (OUTPUT) where buffered areas are burned in with value 1 (default behavior of qgis:rasterize), and the count of input features (NUMBEROFFEATURES). All processing is performed locally via QGIS Processing algorithms ('native:buffer' and 'qgis:rasterize'), with no Earth Engine server-side computation — despite the prompt referencing GEE, the script is purely QGIS-based and contains zero ee.* calls or GEE dependencies.

Identify dangle overlap status. The script identifies dangles (unconnected line endpoints) in a user-provided vector line layer using the 'Continuous_Network_Analysis:Identify Dangles' algorithm. It then buffers selected project layers (points, lines, and polygons) by 0.000001 decimal degrees, merges the buffered geometries, and performs spatial intersection and non-intersection operations to classify dangles into two outputs: (1) 'DANGLES_Overlapping' — dangles that intersect/overlap with any of the selected layers, and (2) 'DANGLES_Non_Overlap' — dangles that do not intersect/overlap with any selected layer. The output layers preserve original dangle attributes and add a 'layer_overlap' field indicating which overlapping layer contributed to the match.

Minority language spatial scoring. The script processes minority language points and language area polygons to compute a scoring model. It overlays minority language points with type A and type B language polygons to extract intersecting language codes. It calculates the maximum distance to the minimal bounding circle of each type A language polygon (D) and the minimum distance to the polygon boundary (b), then computes D-b and a function fx(a) = 21.6679 * ln(101 - 100*(D-b)/D). It also extracts up to three type B language codes from overlaps and retrieves their confidence scores from an external table. The output is a vector layer with added fields including overlap lists, distances, scores, and concatenated confidence values.

Compute slope-based terrain inclination classes. The script computes terrain slope from DGM (Digital Ground Model) raster data, classifies slope values into five inclination classes (1–5) based on mean slope per polygon (Einzelflächen), and writes both the class ID ('neigkl') and mean slope value ('neigung') back to the 'flaechen' table in the QKan SQLite database. Key steps include: (1) reprojecting the 'Einzelflächen' vector layer to a target EPSG; (2) determining DGM tile coordinates (1 km grid) covering the layer’s bounding box; (3) downloading DGM1-32 tiles (e.g., 'dgm1_32_x_y_1_nw*') via HTTP directory listing parsing; (4) merging downloaded GeoTIFFs into a single 'dgm_gesamt.tif'; (5) computing slope raster ('neigung.tif'); (6) performing zonal statistics to extract mean slope per polygon; (7) classifying mean slope using nested 'if' expression thresholds (≤1°→1, ≤4°→2, ≤10°→3, ≤14°→4, >14°→5); and (8) updating the 'neigkl' and 'neigung' fields in the database-linked 'flaechen' layer.

Calculate multi-buffer accessibility distances. The script computes concentric isochrones (distance-based or time-based) around point features (e.g., health facilities, schools) using QGIS native network analysis on a road network layer. For National/Local scales, it generates non-overlapping distance bands (e.g., 500m, 1000m, 2000m) via sequential difference operations on dissolved isochrones, then assigns inverted distance scores (5 for closest band, 1 for farthest). For Regional scale, it uses simple Euclidean buffering and scores grid cells (e.g., H3 hexagons) based on percentage intersection with the buffer, mapping overlap percentages to discrete scores via configurable thresholds. Outputs are rasterized layers per study area, combined into a VRT; intermediate outputs include clipped road networks, isochrone GeoPackages, band layers, and scored vector grids.

Vectorize Elevation Threshold Polygons. The script processes a raster elevation model by applying a threshold to extract areas below (or above) a specified elevation value. It then vectorizes these areas into polygons, smoothing, simplifying, and removing small polygons. The final output is a GeoPackage layer with area attributes, suitable for floodplain mapping or terrain analysis.

QGIS workflow: Data processing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing. This workflow contains 5 core geospatial operations, including Data processing, Data Acquisition And Preprocessing, Data editing, Buffer Analysis. The description is derived deterministically from retained operator records because no descriptive-knowledge record was available.

Rasterize tabular data from distribution maps. The algorithm distributes the values of all numeric fields from a source table onto raster maps based on a polygon distribution map and a reference raster's georeferencing. It joins the table to the vector layer using a common ID field, then rasterizes each numeric field into ASCII raster files, outputting them to a specified folder.

Select agricultural land patches near urban fabric. The script processes Urban Atlas 2018 land cover data for Poznan, Poland, to select agricultural and other land cover patches within the urban core. It first clips the land cover layer to the urban core mask, then extracts areas with codes 21000 (arable land), 22000 (permanent crops), 23000 (pastures), 24000 (complex cultivation), and 13400 (land without current use) as selected areas. It also extracts urban fabric classes (11100, 11210-11240) as attached areas and railway areas (12230) as detached areas. Buffers of 200 m are applied to attached areas and 250 m to detached areas, and the selected areas are intersected with the attached buffer then differenced with the detached buffer. The resulting polygons are split into single parts and filtered to retain only those with an area >= 10 hectares. The final layer is added to the QGIS project.

Compute minimum distance buffers for points. The script computes a distance matrix for a point layer against itself to find the minimum distance for each point to its nearest other point (using statistics). It then creates circular buffers around each point with a radius equal to that minimum distance. The result is a polygon layer added to the QGIS project.

Buffer-based polygon interior-exterior partitioning. The script partitions a polygon layer (RPFGC_PPSM) into interior and exterior regions relative to a buffer of another layer (RVFundamental). It creates a buffer of distance 20 around RVFundamental, clips the buffer to RPFGC_PPSM to obtain interior areas, computes the difference between RPFGC_PPSM and interior to get exterior areas, then merges both into a single output layer. The result is exported as a GeoPackage file.

Identify suitable school locations. The script identifies suitable areas for new schools by spatially analyzing population density, proximity to existing schools, and proximity to rivers within a user-defined administrative boundary.
